display.title: Episode 468: The Napkins and Toothpicks, Chapter 2 (Purim)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Purim-eve show: a guide to Taanis Esther and the Purim mitzvos, the funny ending of the toothpicks-and-needles parable, and why every Purim mitzvah builds achdus.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the night before Taanis Esther 5751. Uncle Yossi wishes everyone a happy Purim, groggers ready, and lays out the schedule: the fast on Wednesday with extra tzedakah, the Megillah Wednesday night and Thursday morning, mishloach manos of at least two ready-to-eat foods, matanos la'evyonim, and the Purim seudah with friends and relatives, plus the Tzivos Hashem Purim missions. The Hakochainik march is sung l'kavod Purim. A yeshiva student leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time concludes the rabbi's parable for the king. The father sends the useless toothpicks and needles to the fair with two expert salesmen, Mr. Reuben and Mr. Brown, who meet as strangers and simply swap loads, so both come home with the same goods. The father explains that his son traded precious gold for junk, while the salesmen only traded one worthless thing for another: so too, a Jew who leaves Hashem for idols loses something priceless, while other nations only swap one idol for another. Uncle Yossi closes by showing how the Megillah reading, mishloach manos, gifts to the poor and the seudah all build achdus.
display.lesson: Never trade the priceless gift of Hashem and His Torah for something worthless; and Purim's mitzvos teach us to live in unity.
